commits.message:
expectLinearTime's own tests read a verdict off simulated time, and its real ones spend stated CPU time (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr) (#523)

* A synchronous test that runs out its time reports its CPU and load, not undefined (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr)

The budget's timer cannot fire while a synchronous test holds the thread, so
the report printed the literal word `undefined` on every such failure. It now
reads the CPU and load when the failure is reported and says the reading covers
the whole run.

* expectLinearTime's own tests read the verdict off simulated time, so no runner can stall them (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr)

The stalled-quadratic test failed five CI runs at 30 s with the file at about
121 s against 8 s, with its timings lost to the timeout. expectLinearTime takes
its stopwatch as an argument, and six of the seven tests spend stated
milliseconds, so a verdict is arithmetic and each states exact sizes. The test
that the clock counts CPU and not wall time keeps the real one, and no longer
asserts the size it settled on.

* expectLinearTime's real tests spend stated CPU time, and a timeout report stops guessing why no timer fired (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr)

The test left on the real clock cost steps, so a floor trip took about 27 s of
its 30 s budget and silently dropped what it proved. Its cost is now CPU time,
which cannot fall under the floor or grow, and a second real test fails
quadratic work through the default stopwatch, the one false pass nothing else
would see: a cumulative clock read every ratio as 1 and passed every guard.

timeout-report said a test held the thread whenever its timer had not fired, but
a hook running out a shorter budget has not fired it either. The guidance beside
it already tells the two apart from the CPU reading, so the sentence goes.

The header's 'load cannot trip the floor' goes too: the five failures this ticket
is about are the only evidence, and they put it in doubt.

* expectLinearTime says when it grows, and its off-CPU test waits on a measured burn (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr)

A floor trip left no trace: its timings were dropped by the continue, which is
why this ticket's cause could not be established. It now warns with them, and
that reaches a CI log on a pass and on a timeout alike.

The off-CPU test's fixed wait read under the bar in wall time once a loaded
thread got less than half a core, so the guard was weakest on the machine it
models. The wait is twice the measured burn again, and a wall clock fails it
beside 48 spinners.

* The real stopwatch's unit is pinned, and no caller grows on an ordinary run (rich-unfiled-791c.6uvr)

Nothing tested the floor against the real clock, so a stopwatch reading
microseconds passed every test and let every real caller measure fixed costs.
A run of 2 ms must now read under the floor and one of 8 ms over it.

Five callers tripped the floor every run, so the new warning fired on green.
Their sizes are now about what they grew to, and a warning is news.

A reading taken as the failure is reported now says so, since after-hooks are
in it.
